summary: University of the People (UoPeople) is a US-accredited online university that charges no tuition. You pay a $60 application fee and an assessment fee for each course ($180 per undergraduate course; $430–$490 per graduate course), and donor scholarships can cover part of these. It suits motivated self-starters with a secondary-school certificate (or a bachelor's for master's) who need a flexible, low-cost degree while working or living anywhere.
lookfor: Proof you finished secondary school (or a bachelor's for master's programmes)
Proof of English proficiency, or completing UoPeople's English course
Passing up to five Foundation courses with a GPA of at least 2.0 before becoming a degree student
For the MBA: two years' full-time work experience and one recommendation letter
For fee scholarships: genuine financial need and keeping a GPA of 2.0 or higher
cycle: Five terms a year. Next deadlines: 22 Oct 2026 (term starts 12 Nov), 7 Jan 2027 (starts 28 Jan), 18 Mar 2027 (starts 8 Apr), 27 May 2027 (starts 17 Jun). Early-admission deadlines are three weeks earlier.

eligibility.q: Have you completed secondary school (e.g. WAEC/NECO certificate) and can you show the certificate?
eligibility.no: Without a certificate you may still qualify by passing an Ability to Benefit test; check the catalog.

eligibility.q: For a master's: do you hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution?
eligibility.no: Start with a UoPeople associate or bachelor's degree instead.

eligibility.q: Can you show English proficiency (degree taught in English, 30+ college credits in English, or a test such as TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo)?
eligibility.no: You can take UoPeople's English course through the portal instead; plan for one extra term.

eligibility.q: For the MBA: do you have at least two years of full-time work experience?
eligibility.no: Consider the M.Ed. or MSIT (check their requirements) or gain experience first.

eligibility.q: Are you 18 or older (required for graduate programmes)?
eligibility.no: Check the undergraduate rules for younger applicants.

eligibility.q: Do you have a computer or smartphone, reliable internet and steady study time every week for each course?
eligibility.no: Plan access (cyber café, data bundle, work laptop) before you start; courses are weekly and deadline-driven.

eligibility.q: Will a US-accredited online degree be accepted for your goal (job, NYSC, further study, professional licence)?
eligibility.no: Check with your employer, licensing body or (in Nigeria) the NUC before enrolling.

steps.title: Decide if a tuition-free online degree fits you
steps.why: UoPeople is low-cost, not free; you will pay assessment fees and need self-discipline to finish.
do: Open UoPeople's fees page and note the total for your programme (e.g. Bachelor's in Business or Computer Science about $7,260; General Studies about $4,000; MBA about $5,940).
Divide by the number of terms you plan to study to get a cost per term.
Check that the degree will be recognised for your goal (employer, regulator, further study).
Choose your programme: associate, bachelor's, MBA, M.Ed. or MSIT.
tips: Most students pay one course at a time ($180 per undergraduate course), so cost is spread out.
avoid: Telling family it is 'completely free'—assessment fees are real costs.
check: I know my total cost and how I will pay per term.

steps.title: Pick your start term and build a timeline
steps.why: Supporting documents (like English proof) are due by the application deadline, not later.
do: Open the academic calendar and choose your start term.
If 22 October is too soon, aim for 7 January 2027 (early deadline 17 December 2026).
Set reminders: documents ready one week before the deadline; application fee paid three days before.
tips: Use the early deadline; late applications are processed only if time allows.
avoid: Applying the day before term starts and missing the 'save your spot' date.
check: My chosen term and its deadline are in my calendar.

steps.title: Scan your certificates and ID
steps.why: You need proof of secondary-school completion (or your bachelor's) to become a degree student.
do: Scan your secondary-school certificate (e.g. WAEC/NECO) in colour, or get a certified black-and-white copy.
Master's applicants: scan your bachelor's certificate and transcript.
Scan a government ID or passport.
Save each as a clear PDF named by type (e.g. Surname_WAEC.pdf).
tips: If your original certificate is not yet collected, start now; schools can take weeks to release them.
avoid: Uploading a WAEC result checker printout when the certificate is required—check what the portal accepts.
check: All scans are readable and complete.

steps.title: Prepare your English proof
steps.why: Non-native speakers must show English proficiency by the application deadline, or take UoPeople's English course.
do: Check if you qualify through a degree taught in English or 30+ semester credits with a C average.
Otherwise use a TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo score.
If you have none, plan to take the English course offered in the portal.
Upload the proof in the portal; appeals are also made there.
tips: Duolingo is usually the cheapest and fastest test to take from home.
avoid: Booking a test that cannot deliver results before the deadline.
check: I have accepted English proof or a plan to take the course.

steps.title: Master's only: CV, work proof and recommender
steps.why: The MBA requires two years' full-time work and one formal recommendation letter.
do: Write a short CV with your jobs, dates and duties.
Ask a manager or lecturer for a formal recommendation letter.
Note the recommender's name, email and phone number with country code—the form asks for them.
tips: Choose a recommender who can speak to both your work and your ability to study online.
avoid: Counting NYSC or part-time jobs as full-time experience without checking the rules.
check: I have my recommender's full contact details and agreement.

steps.title: Fill in the online application form
steps.why: This short form creates your portal account.
do: Go to uopeople.edu and click Apply.
Enter contact details and choose your programme.
Submit; you will get portal login details by email.
Log in and review your information; correct any mistakes yourself.
tips: Use the same name spelling as on your certificates.
avoid: Using an email you rarely check.
check: I can log in to the student portal.

steps.title: Pay the $60 application fee
steps.why: Your application is not processed until the fee is paid.
do: In the portal, open the payment section.
Pay $60 by card, PayPal, Western Union or Convera.
Save the receipt.
tips: Nigerian naira cards often have foreign spending limits; check yours or use a dollar card or Western Union.
avoid: Paying through a third party who is not an official payment channel.
check: The portal shows the fee as paid.

steps.title: Complete your admissions pathway in the portal
steps.why: The portal asks personalised questions; English proof and transfer transcripts must be in by the deadline.
do: Answer the English proficiency questions and upload your proof (or choose the English course).
If you studied at university before, upload full transcripts for a free transfer-credit check.
Upload your secondary-school (or bachelor's) certificate.
Submit and watch your email for the decision.
tips: Transfer credits can shorten your degree and cut costs; upload all past transcripts.
check: Every portal task is marked complete.

steps.title: Request a fee scholarship (if you need one)
steps.why: Scholarships are not automatic and are given first-come, first-served each term.
do: After acceptance, open the Funding page in your portal.
Choose to apply for a scholarship instead of paying yourself.
Answer the questions about your situation honestly and clearly (who supports you, monthly income, why you need help, your study goal).
If approved, click 'Secure my Scholarship Now'.
tips: Apply as soon as you are accepted; funds run out.
Some funds target groups such as refugees, women or certain countries—read the list.
avoid: Applying for more than one scholarship at a time (not allowed).
Expecting a scholarship if you already hold a degree—UoPeople generally does not award them to degree holders.
check: My scholarship request is submitted or secured.
steps.prompt: Explain your financial situation and why support will help you complete your studies (questions shown in the portal).
steps.limit: Check the current guidance in the portal

steps.title: Sign the agreement and save your spot
steps.why: Your place in the Foundation courses is held only after you sign by the 'last day to save spot'.
do: Read the online enrolment/introductory course agreement.
Sign it digitally in the portal within the time given (often 7 days).
Complete the required orientation course before term starts.
tips: Read the withdrawal and fee rules before signing.
avoid: Missing the save-your-spot date (e.g. 12 Nov 2026 for Term 2).
check: My agreement is signed and orientation is done.

steps.title: Pass your Foundation courses
steps.why: You become a degree student only after passing up to five Foundation courses with a GPA of 2.0 or above.
do: Log in every week; each course has weekly discussion posts, assignments and peer assessments.
Block fixed study hours in your week for each course (check the course syllabus for the expected workload).
Take one or two courses per term at first.
Pay each course's assessment fee (or use your scholarship) on time.
tips: Write down each week's deadlines in your local time zone.
avoid: Taking too many courses while working full-time.

steps.title: Send official documents and become a degree student
steps.why: Official proof must arrive by week 6 of the term before you start as a degree student.
do: Arrange for your official diploma/transcript to reach UoPeople, or upload a colour/certified scan as allowed.
Confirm in the portal that documents are accepted.
Keep your GPA at 2.0 or above to keep any scholarship.
tips: Start this in your first Foundation term so you never lose a term waiting.
avoid: Sending documents late and having to pause your studies.
check: The portal shows me as a degree student.

faq.a: Tuition is free, but you pay a $60 application fee and an assessment fee per course ($180 per undergraduate course).

faq.q: Do I need to write an essay?
faq.a: Undergraduate admission has no essay. You may explain your situation when requesting a scholarship in the portal. The MBA needs one recommendation letter.

faq.q: Can I get a scholarship before I am accepted?
faq.a: No. You request it on the Funding page after acceptance, and funds are first-come, first-served.
Yes. Courses are online and asynchronous, but each has weekly deadlines.

faq.q: Will my degree be recognised in my country?
faq.a: UoPeople is US-accredited, but recognition depends on your employer or regulator. Check before enrolling (in Nigeria, ask the NUC or your employer).
